title: Destiny 2’s Returning Content Makes This The Perfect Time To Grab Its Complete DLC Bundle
summary: I have a love-hate relationship with Destiny 2 . I love the game and hate the fact that most of the content from Forsaken and before has essentially vanished, making it harder to recommend to newcomers. With active development set to end after the release of Renegades in The Fate Saga, the fact that much of The Light and Darkness Saga was unplayable was a sad fate. Now, Bungie is bringing back older content, sweeping open the door to the vault, and that means getting the entire Destiny 2 experience at a low price is worth picking up. Destiny 2 is at its best when you can play through the entire narrative, from The Red War onward. Of course, Destiny 1 being limited to older-generation consoles isn't brilliant, but the fact that most of the saga is in the sequel makes it mostly fine. Yet Bungie's vaulting of previously playable Destiny 2 content was never a great move. Since the announcement that the game was no longer receiving content, I had stopped playing. Now, this gives me and many other Guardians a chance to play again, and for newcomers, it means not missing out on valuable lore. It would take me a long time to explain the lore, but basically, a white ball in the sky resurrects warriors to fight against darkness; you are one of those warriors. You choose which class you want to play as, between Hunter, Warlock, or Titan—each with its own strengths—and battle enemies across the solar system. Oh, and you need to farm for loot, including the coveted Exotic gear, which consists of game-changing pieces of equipment that can help you build a powerful Guardian. https://www.youtube.com/live/v3mXEsZIlmU It's one of the best FPS games out there. Bungie's gunplay remains solid and consistent a decade after release, and Destiny 2 is still one of my favorite looters to play. Shredding hordes of Vex is as satisfying as it has ever been. The DLCs are easily some of the best in the genre, with The Witch Queen and The Final Shape being some of the greatest expansions in gaming—our Final Shape review is proof of that. So, when you can get potentially hundreds of hours of content for a fraction of the price, it's not something to pass on. Right now, you can grab the entire Destiny 2 experience (once content is unvaulted) for just $16.10 / £13.34 at Fanatical . That includes every post-launch release and update, giving you a genre-defining experience for a low price. And you get to hear the late Lance Reddick's voice once again. So whether you're a returning Guardian wanting the full experience or a New Light willing to give it a shot, you have no excuse now. Disclosure: GameSpot and Fanatical are both owned by Fandom. This story was created in collaboration with Fanatical’s deals team.

title: GTA 6’s Furry Rescue Mission Is A Little Weird, But The Rewards Are Worth It
summary: No matter what you do in GTA 6 , it pales in comparison to being a Furry in that game. Anyone looking to externalize their inner animal spirit is in danger of being hunted, and you'll find out for yourself just how much the fictional state of Leonida hates Furries when you're given the chance to save one of them from being murdered by the cops. Should you help them? Absolutely, if you want an easy payday or a new weapon for your arsenal. How to find Chase the Fox Like several other missions in GTA 6, helping out the Furry resistance appears to trigger randomly. The mission takes place after Chapter 3, on Miramar Drive in Crosstown, Vice City, and you'll want to be cruising around that area at night, between midnight and 4 AM. Once it starts, you'll see cops pull up to hunt down a Furry by the name of Chase, and if you drive up to him, you can either give him a lift or leave him to his brutal fate. Outrun the cops If you do choose to help Chase, then get ready to be hunted down by cops. You'll pick up a three-star Wanted level, which means the cops will be in mildly hot pursuit of your vehicle. Reach the parking garage Chase will direct you to a nearby parking garage, where his Furry allies are waiting. After a short standoff, they'll welcome you into their ranks as an honorary Furry. Courier the group to safety To get the law off your polyester tail, one of your new allies will take your car and use it to distract the cops. Get inside the van, and you can bring the other Furries home to their swanky pad in Starfish Island. While you're driving, the Furries will interact with each other, and you can watch their hijinks. Choose your reward Once Chase and his pals are back home, you'll be offered one of two rewards: $15,000 in cash or the unique Furry DW-9 submachine gun. Personally, I'd go with the gun since it's easy enough to make cash in GTA 6, and having more weapons is never a bad idea. You'll also gain safehouse access to the Furry group's hideout, where you can stock up on weapons and body armor. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

title: How To Get The Anime Car In GTA 6
summary: There are a few ways to get an anime car in GTA 6 , but if you don't want to spend any money, we've stumbled upon one just there for the taking. There's no huge mission or shootout to survive; in fact the car owner is randomly rolled when you enter the house. Ours belongs to a guy partaking in some extracurricular activities via the medium of VR. Sure enough, he's pretty distracted, so this one's an easy grab. We've also heard of blindfolded men tied to the bed, and other spicy scenarios. You'll want to head to Ambrosia, although we've heard of the car spawning in other locations around Key Lento, too. The house in question is right across the road from a garage. The house is marked on our location in this screenshot. The car is in the garage, and you can just walk in and take it. While this particular anime livery is exclusive to the Declasse Akane, you can take some cars to Tuners mod shops, since they specialize in JDM vehicles, or Vice Auto Customs, where some anime liveries are available to apply to your car. You'll find the anime car inside the garage. Be careful taking this car anywhere for work though--don't touch the customization menu or the wrap might be overwritten, and there's no way of getting it back. If you're wondering which of the hundreds of random activities to attempt next, or maybe you're looking for a specific weapon, check out our GTA 6 guides hub .

title: Mario, Pikachu, And Other Gaming Icon Balloons Won’t Be Flying This Thanksgiving
summary: New York City is no stranger to bad weather, be it blazing-hot summers, snow-packed winters, or fierce windstorms. Unfortunately for countless families who have made it a holiday tradition to turn on the TV and watch giant totems of pop culture sail in the streets of the great city, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been officially delayed due to a forecast of rain and windstorms--a first in its 100-year history. In recent years, gaming icons have become more and more prominent during the parade. Beginning in 1993, a balloon of Sonic the Hedgehog marked the first game character to float among the procession. Since then, more characters have joined the festivities, including Mario, Pac-Man, Pikachu, and even Red the Angry Bird, among others. However, those who have followed the history of Macy's balloons know that the mix of bad weather and massive, floating objects can result in genuine danger for balloon handlers, bystanders, and objects on the streets. Rather infamously, Sonic's 1993 appearance was marred by an incident where the balloon got stuck on a lamppost, popping the balloon and injuring two bystanders. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DmTC0m7wQbs Other balloon bursts have proved even more catastrophic, with a series of mishaps in 1997 leading to a Cat in the Hat balloon causing injuries that left a woman comatose for days . Since then, more emphasis has rightfully been put on safety. While it might be disappointing to not be able to point at the TV and go "Mario!" with your younger cousins around the TV tomorrow, the balloons will get a chance to fly on Saturday starting at 8:30 AM ET, when the weather is likely to be significantly less awful. You can find other ways to fill the time--but maybe ask your relatives first if it's okay to let the kiddos watch you play GTA 6. Image credit: Getty Images / Craig T Fruchtman

title: Nearly Three Decades And Four Consoles Later, I Finally Beat Ocarina Of Time
summary: I finally did it. As Princess Zelda held the transformed, monstrous Ganon in place with her magic, I delivered the final blow with the Master Sword. The Demon King was sealed away and Hyrule was saved. I found myself getting emotional, because this was the first time in 28 years that I had beaten The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. For many, that would mean it was also the first time they had played Ocarina of Time, but this wasn't the case for me. I first played the game, if you can call running around Kokiri Forest "playing the game," back around launch in 1998, when I was four years old. It was my older brother's Nintendo 64, and his copy of the game, which he had already completed. My adventures in Hyrule primarily consisted of exploring Hyrule Field and switching between the child and adult timelines. I even loved flipping through my brother's strategy guide to the point that my mom got it spiral bound at Kinko's. But I never made any progress. The animation of Link pulling the Master Sword from its marble resting place was mesmerizing to me, but to be completely honest … Ganondorf terrified me too much to want to actually face him in the climactic battle. I distinctly remember a moment at summer camp a short time later, when each camper was asked to share a fear. Some were afraid of snakes. Some picked spiders or the dark. I said "Ganondorf" without a second thought, and I meant it. He was terrifying! His evil smirk when looking down on Link as he chased Zelda and Impa out of the castle was burned into my brain. Terrifying I started and ultimately fizzled out on a few more playthroughs on Nintendo 64, and eventually picked up a new version of Ocarina of Time for GameCube a few years later--the Legend of Zelda: Collector's Edition, which was pretty much the same experience but with a better controller. Still, I found myself struggling to get any further, and I put the game aside in favor of Super Smash Bros. I sure wish I hadn't opened it, too, considering how ridiculously valuable it is today . It would be many years before I made another attempt, this time on 3DS. This version was marketed as a big improvement over the original Nintendo 64 release, and it's hard to deny that, even from the game's early moments. The motion controls on 3DS made aiming the slingshot remarkably easy, and the much-needed visual overhaul made the characters seem more like people. But still, despite loving what I played, I drifted away. This time, it was shortly after finishing the Forest Temple, and though I planned to go back and finish the rest of the game, that never happened. As the years passed, I had resigned myself to the fact, or what I thought was a fact, that I would never finish Ocarina of Time. I still had a great appreciation for what it brought to the medium, but I wasn't champing at the bit to give it another try. That was, of course, until Nintendo decided to remake the game again, this time on Nintendo Switch 2. Caught up in the excitement of so many of my friends and colleagues playing Ocarina of Time again, I decided to give it another shot--and to be completely honest, I wasn't sure things would be any different this time. Maybe it was everyone around me getting caught up in the excitement of playing Ocarina of Time together. Maybe it was being able to sing the songs instead of having to press the buttons. It might have just been that the game had less friction this time, with the motion-controlled aiming and movable camera just making it more enjoyable to play. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_xMM7L2XoMc It was likely some combination of all of these factors that kept me hooked past when I would usually burn out and move on to a different game. After making it past the Forest Temple, Fire Temple, and Water Temple, it occurred to me that I was actually nearing the final battle with Ganondorf. A few hours later, I had all the Sages on board, and I made my way into Ganondorf's imposing tower. Just from absorbing gaming pop-culture over the years, I knew to expect his aggressive organ music as I climbed to the top, but it still felt monumental. Frankly, I even already knew the strategy for beating him, but finally getting to do it myself--and then deliver the "real" final blow against his monstrous Ganon form--was like finally closing a chapter in my life. Ocarina of Time was one of the first video games I can remember watching someone play, and I probably would never have finally seen the credits roll if this remake didn't exist. Thanks, Nintendo.

title: Rockstar Games Has A GTA 6 Hit On Its Hands, But Its Union Vote Is A Loss
summary: Roughly 75% of Rockstar Games staff in the UK have voted against a formal recognition agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB). The news came in the wake of GTA 6 's record-breaking launch , and had the IWGB been recognized, Rockstar Games management would have been legally obligated to negotiate collective bargaining terms with the union on topics such as pay, hours, and conditions. Voting took place across two weeks, and turnout was massive, with over 93% of UK staff casting their ballot (roughly 1,544 employees). The IWGB said it was undeterred by the result and would continue working to build support among Rockstar employees. "While the result means Rockstar will not be formally required to hold regular meetings with union representatives under a recognition agreement, it does not prevent workers from continuing to organize and push for workplace improvements through the IWGB, joining the union or exercising their individual trade union rights and protections," the union said in a statement. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GVyCl_Euhmo The vote also comes hot on the heels of the IWGB taking Rockstar to an employment tribunal, alleging unlawful dismissal and union busting after it fired over 30 employees last year for gross misconduct over alleged leaks of confidential information. Closing submissions were wrapped up shortly before the vote results came out, and a ruling is still pending. While game dev unionizing has gained significant momentum over the years, a decisive loss at one of the industry's biggest studios could be a notable speed bump for union organizers. With Rockstar also riding the wave of GTA 6's monumental success, employees may be focused on bonuses and post-launch momentum, which could make pushing through a formal union structure even harder. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society--this isn't a sign to retreat; it's a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favor of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues,' the IWGB added.

title: You Can Find Lucia’s Discarded Gun From The GTA 6 Prologue
summary: In the prologue sequence for GTA 6 , Lucia finds herself in a bit of trouble, forced to discard a handgun she'd used to hold up a store. However, it's not lost forever. You can return to the store and find the gun nearby, but this is easier to do in Chapter 3, once you've made it to Vice City. To find the gun, you'll want to head to the Little Cuba area of Vice City, just off the large highway. There's an area with Rosita's Cuban Cafe and the payday loans shop that Lucia holds up. The gun isn't found on the street; you'll have to take to the rooftops and search for it. The pink marker shows where Lucia's gun can be picked up. Climb to the roof of the payday loans store and head toward the canal. Look for the air conditioning units and a round metal vent. You'll find the beaten up Low Point Nipper .38 on top of the vent itself. We were playing as Lucia when we picked it up, but it unlocks for her and Jason once you've collected it. Lucia's gun is on top of the vent nearby. For more on the weird goings-on around Leonida, from alien sightings to a free tank, check out our GTA 6 guides hub .
